title: Plugins
subtitle: Manage the local Codex plugins bundled with mimo2codex. Environment variables take precedence over the admin toggle.

notice.title: Pure Node — no compiler toolchain required
notice.desc: The toggle writes the built-in MCP server into your Codex config. Desktop control is driven by nut.js (mouse/keyboard/screenshot) — just npm install, no git/.NET/Xcode. Vision models act on the screenshot; text-only models act on OCR'd text coordinates. Electron is optional and draws a glowing cursor on the real desktop.

envLocked.title: {{envKey}} is set; the admin toggle is read-only
envLocked.desc: The effective value is: {{value}}. To manage it from the admin UI, remove the variable and restart mimo2codex.

configMismatch.title: Plugin state differs from the Codex config
configMismatch.desc: It's expected to be enabled, but config.toml has no matching MCP server yet. Click refresh, or toggle the switch once.

usage.title: How to use it after enabling
usage.desc: Restart Codex CLI / Desktop and the model can see computer_state, computer_click, computer_type, computer_key, computer_scroll, computer_wait, and computer_install_adapter MCP tools. Watch the AI act live on the "Computer Use Monitor" page.
usage.prompt: Please call computer_state, look at the screen, then click/operate for me.

msg.enabled: Plugin enabled and Codex config updated; restart Codex to load it.
msg.disabled: Plugin disabled and removed from Codex config.

learnMore: Read the plugin intro on docweb

contribute.title: Contribute a plugin
contribute.desc: Built a fun computer-use / MCP plugin adapter? Submit it on docweb — once accepted it shows up here.

adapter.title: Desktop-control dependencies (pure Node)
adapter.desc: nut.js is the core backend (mouse/keyboard/screenshot, prebuilt, no toolchain). Electron is optional — it draws a glowing cursor on the real desktop.
adapter.withElectronLabel: Also download the glowing-cursor runtime (Electron, large)
adapter.installOkRestart: Installed. Restart Codex so it reloads the plugin.
adapter.uninstallOk: Removed the Electron glowing cursor (nut.js kept — basic control still works). Restart Codex to apply.
adapter.failed: Action failed — check the log above.
adapter.unsupported: This platform isn't supported (nut.js supports macOS and Windows).
adapter.overlayDesc: Shows a glowing cyan cursor and click ripples on the real desktop while the AI works, plus a "Stop AI control" button. Optional — without it everything still works, you just won't see the desktop cursor (you can still watch the Monitor page).
adapter.confirmRemoveElectron: Remove the Electron glowing-cursor runtime? nut.js is kept.
adapter.macPermission: macOS: after install, grant Accessibility + Screen Recording to the host app (terminal / Codex) in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
